# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Sovex Seed Distribution, LLC (Supervising Attorney)
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 10, 2026
**Re:** Sovex / Ludis Genetics: review of the supply paperwork, priority issues and recommended fixes

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed four documents:

- the Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2026 (the **SA**);
- Order Form No. 2 for the 2026–2027 Season, dated April 20, 2026 (**OF2**);
- the Data Processing Addendum dated January 15, 2026 (the **DPA**); and
- the Hartwell Agribusiness cover letter dated February 10, 2026, which encloses Sovex's certificate of insurance (the **Broker Letter**).

Key commercial facts:

- **Governing law and forum.** The SA is governed by New York law, with exclusive jurisdiction in the courts of New York County (SA §19.1).
- **Term.** The Initial Term ends on **December 31, 2028** (SA §2.1).
- **The deal.** OF2 covers Ludis proprietary hybrid corn only (five LG varieties in Exhibit A). The resale **Territory is Iowa and Nebraska** (OF2 §2.2).
- **Volumes.** 48,000 units are ordered. The Minimum Purchase Commitment is 40,000 units, with a shortfall rate of $42/unit (OF2 §3).
- **Liability cap.** The cap is the Fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months (SA §12.1).

Five issues need attention, listed in order of exposure:

| # | Issue | Location | Exposure | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Uncapped Grower Claims indemnity, including claims caused by Ludis's own seed | SA §11.2, §1.6, §12.3(a) | Unlimited; existential | High. Live each season |
| 2 | Germination notice on Order Form No. 1 sent late; Ludis has rejected it | OF2 Recital B and §7; SA §8.4 | Value of the March 30 Claim, plus the same trap on 2027 deliveries | High. 2027 tranches begin January 15, 2027 |
| 3 | Exclusivity covers corn, soybean and sorghum across the U.S. and Canada | SA §4.1 (with §19.2; OF2 §2.2) | Possible current breach; loss of other product lines | High. May already be in breach |
| 4 | DPA sets Iowa law and a Polk County forum for disputes about the whole Agreement | DPA §12 (vs. SA §19.1, §19.2) | Split law and forum; parallel litigation | Medium |
| 5 | Automatic three-year renewals with a 30-day opt-out window | SA §2.2 | Lock-in to 2031 | Medium. Window opens August 2028 |

Open questions for the client are collected in Section 4.

---

## 2. Issues (highest exposure first)

### Issue 1: Uncapped indemnity for all Grower Claims, whatever the cause

**Where:**
- SA §11.2, Customer indemnity
- SA §1.6, definition of "Grower Claims"
- SA §12.3(a), carve-out from the cap and from the consequential-damages exclusion

**What it says.**
- Under §11.2, Sovex must defend and indemnify Ludis against any claim "arising out of or relating to Customer's use, handling, storage, resale or planting of Products, *including any Grower Claims*."
- §1.6 defines Grower Claims as any grower claim relating to "crop stand, emergence, yield or performance of Products, *whatever the cause*."
- §12.3(a) then removes "a Party's *obligations under Section 11*" from both the §12.1 cap and the §12.2 exclusion of consequential damages and lost profits.

**Why it matters for Sovex.**

*1. Sovex carries the risk of Ludis's own bad seed.* Take a lot that is genetically or physically defective when Ludis ships it, for example one with low germination or a treatment failure. Growers who plant it and lose stand or yield will typically sue Sovex as their seller, and they may also sue Ludis. Because the definition reaches claims "whatever the cause," Sovex must defend Ludis and pay Ludis's losses even where Ludis caused them.

*2. There is no ceiling on the amount.*
- The carve-out in §12.3(a) looks mutual, but it is not mutual in practice. Ludis's only indemnity (§11.1) is a narrow IP infringement indemnity.
- The carve-out therefore uncaps Sovex's crop-failure exposure and does almost nothing for Sovex in return.
- Crop-loss claims are measured in lost bushels across thousands of acres. A single bad lot can produce losses far above the 12-month-Fees cap. On OF2 alone, Fees are roughly $14–15 million.
- Lost profits and consequential losses are also back in play, because §12.2 is carved out as well.

*3. Sovex's own warranty remedy does not offset this.* Against Ludis, Sovex's only remedy is replacement or a credit or refund of the Fees for the nonconforming units (§8.6). Ludis also disclaims yield warranties (§8.7). So Sovex can owe Ludis unlimited indemnity for a defect while recovering only the seed price from Ludis.

*4. Insurance may not fill the gap.* The Broker Letter confirms $5M per occurrence and a $10M products-completed operations aggregate. That meets SA §13.1.
- However, CGL policies commonly exclude or limit pure economic loss, "impaired property" and "your product" claims, and contractually assumed liability beyond an "insured contract."
- The Broker Letter also confirms that Ludis is an *additional insured* on Sovex's policy (Vendors endorsement). In effect, Sovex's policy limits are being shared with the party whose seed may have caused the loss.

**Recommended fix.**

*(a) Carve Supplier-caused claims out of §11.2 and add a reciprocal product indemnity from Ludis.* Proposed language:

> **11.2 By Customer.** Customer will defend Supplier … against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) Customer's improper storage or handling of Products in breach of Section 7.4, (b) any warranty or representation made by Customer to a Grower in breach of Section 8.8, or (c) Customer's negligence or willful misconduct, and will indemnify … *Customer has no obligation under this Section 11.2 for any claim, including any Grower Claim, to the extent caused by (i) Products that did not conform to the warranty in Section 8.1, (ii) the genetics, traits or seed treatment of the Products, or (iii) Supplier's breach of this Agreement, negligence or willful misconduct.*
>
> **11.1A Product Indemnity by Supplier.** Supplier will defend Customer … against any third-party claim, including any Grower Claim, to the extent arising out of (i) Products that did not conform to the warranty in Section 8.1, (ii) the genetics, traits, labeling or seed treatment of the Products, or (iii) Supplier's negligence or willful misconduct, and will indemnify ….

*(b) Fix the definition.* Delete "whatever the cause" from §1.6, or let the allocation language above control.

*(c) Cap Sovex's indemnity.* Amend §12.3(a) to read: "(a) *Supplier's* obligations under Sections 11.1 and 11.1A, and Customer's obligations under Section 11.2 *up to an amount equal to [two (2)] times the cap in Section 12.1*". As a fallback, uncap only the third-party IP and Supplier product indemnities.

*(d) Make Ludis's insurance respond.* Ask Ludis to confirm that its products liability policy names Sovex as an additional insured under SA §13.2 and to deliver its own certificate. The folder contains only Sovex's.

---

### Issue 2: Germination notice on Order Form No. 1 was late and has been rejected; the same window will apply to 2027 deliveries

**Where:**
- OF2 Recital B and §7 (Reservation of Rights)
- SA §8.4

**Timeline.**
- **Delivery Date:** February 20, 2026 (OF2 Recital B).
- **Window:** SA §8.4 requires written notice of any germination shortfall **within 21 days after the Delivery Date**. Otherwise the Products are "deemed accepted as to germination." The window closed on **March 13, 2026**.
- **Notice:** Sovex sent its notice, with laboratory results, on **March 30, 2026**. That is 17 days late.
- **Rejection:** Ludis rejected the notice as untimely by letter dated April 3, 2026.
- **Reservation:** OF2 §7 (signed April 20, 2026) records that Sovex reserves all rights on the March 30 Claim. It also records that signing OF2, ordering under it or paying invoices does not waive the claim.

**Why it matters for Sovex.**

*1. The claim is preserved but contested.* §7 prevents a waiver or estoppel argument based on later dealings. It does not cure lateness. Ludis has a facially strong timeliness defense. Under the contract, the lots are deemed accepted as to germination, and the §8.6 remedies (replacement or credit) are available only for claims "noticed under Section 8.4."

*2. Sovex has a credible counter-argument.* Under N.Y. U.C.C. §1-302(b), the parties may fix time periods by agreement, but only if the period is not *manifestly unreasonable*. U.C.C. §2-607(3)(a) otherwise requires notice within a reasonable time after the buyer discovers or should have discovered the breach. The argument runs as follows:
- Germination shortfalls are latent defects.
- Accredited warm-germ and cold-germ testing, which SA §8.3 expressly contemplates, takes time to schedule and complete. Cold-germ tests in particular run about a week or more before results are read.
- Some shortfalls show up only at emergence, well after 21 days from a February delivery.
- A window that can expire before a diligent buyer could reasonably detect the defect is arguably manifestly unreasonable.

Sovex can also argue that the §8.6 exclusive remedy fails of its essential purpose (U.C.C. §2-719(2)) if a latent defect can never be noticed in time. Both arguments depend on facts, chiefly when Sovex tested, when it received results, and whether the defect could reasonably have been detected earlier.

*3. The problem will recur.* OF2 tranches deliver on January 15, February 12 and March 5, 2027. Under the current §8.4, the notice deadlines will be **February 5, March 5 and March 26, 2027**. Grower-reported emergence problems in spring 2027 will fall outside every one of them. Combined with Issue 1, Sovex could end up indemnifying growers for bad seed while holding no warranty remedy against Ludis.

**Recommended course of action.**

*(a) The March 30 Claim:*
- Preserve evidence: lab reports, chain of custody, testing dates, lot numbers and grower complaints.
- Send a short response to Ludis's April 3 letter. It should state Sovex's position under U.C.C. §§1-302(b) and 2-607(3) and §2-719(2), and refer to the OF2 §7 reservation.
- Consider settling the claim in the renegotiation, for example through credits against OF2 invoices.
- Check limitations. U.C.C. §2-725 gives four years from tender, so there is no near-term bar. Still, avoid drift.

*(b) Amend SA §8.4 before January 15, 2027.* Proposed language:

> **8.4 Germination Claims.** Customer must give Supplier written notice of any claim that Products fail to meet the germination rate in the Specifications within *thirty (30) days after the later of (a) Customer's receipt of warm or cold germination test results from an accredited seed laboratory for the affected lot, provided testing is initiated within thirty (30) days after the Delivery Date, and (b) the date on which Customer first receives a Grower report of emergence or stand failure reasonably attributable to germination, and in any event no later than [July 31] of the Season in which the Products are planted*. Failure to give notice within that period bars the claim only to the extent Supplier is materially prejudiced by the delay.

*(c) Interim protection.* Calendar the 2027 deadlines listed above. Arrange accredited testing of each tranche immediately on delivery.

---

### Issue 3: Exclusivity is far broader than the deal

**Where:** SA §4.1. Read together with SA §19.2 (order of precedence) and OF2 §2.

**What it says.**

| | Scope of the deal | Scope of the §4.1 restriction |
|---|---|---|
| Products | Ludis hybrid corn (Exhibit A) | "any corn, soybean or sorghum seed" from anyone other than Ludis |
| Geography | Iowa and Nebraska | "anywhere in the United States and Canada" |
| Who is bound | Sovex | Sovex "directly or through any Affiliate" |

The restriction covers purchasing, selling and distributing. Under SA §19.2, the SA prevails over an Order Form on non-data matters. The broader §4.1 therefore controls, and the Iowa and Nebraska Territory in OF2 does not narrow it.

**Why it matters for Sovex.**

*1. Sovex may already be in breach.* Most regional distributors carry soybean lines from other breeders, and many carry competing corn brands. If Sovex or an affiliate does either, anywhere, it has arguably been in breach since January 15, 2026. That exposes Sovex to:
- termination for breach under §15.1;
- damages claims; and
- leverage for Ludis in the germination dispute.

*2. Sovex gets little in return.* Ludis's reciprocal commitment (§4.2) is limited to not appointing other distributors for *the Products* in *the Territory*.

*3. Future growth is blocked.* Sovex could not enter adjacent states, or add soybean or sorghum lines, without Ludis's consent for the full Term, including any renewal (see Issue 5).

*4. Antitrust is a secondary point.* A sweeping exclusive-dealing clause with no link to the supplied products carries some competition-law sensitivity. This is not a primary concern at Sovex's likely scale, but it is a useful negotiating point.

**Recommended fix.** Replace §4.1 with the following:

> **4.1 Exclusive Purchasing.** During the Term, Customer shall not purchase for resale, or resell, to Growers *in the Territory* any *hybrid corn seed that competes directly with the Products listed in Exhibit A to the then-current Order Form* from any person other than Supplier. *For clarity, this Section 4.1 does not restrict Customer or its Affiliates from purchasing, selling or distributing (a) soybean, sorghum or any other non-corn seed, (b) any seed outside the Territory, or (c) corn seed of a relative maturity or trait package that Supplier does not offer in the then-current Order Form.*

Also consider adding a right for Sovex to source elsewhere if Ludis cannot supply ordered volumes, or if supply is allocated away from Sovex under §16.2.

---

### Issue 4: DPA governing law and forum conflict with the Supply Agreement

**Where:** DPA §12, which conflicts with SA §19.1. SA §19.2 makes the conflict worse rather than resolving it.

**What it says.**
- DPA §12.1 applies "the *laws of the State of Iowa*" to any dispute "arising out of or relating to this Addendum, *the Agreement* or any processing of Grower Data."
- DPA §12.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts in **Polk County, Iowa**.
- SA §19.1 selects New York law and gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts.
- SA §19.2 says the DPA *prevails* on "data protection matters." So New York is not the default winner. The precedence clause gives the Iowa clause effect for anything that can be characterized as data-related.

**Why it matters for Sovex.**
- There are two competing exclusive-forum clauses, each broad enough on its face to cover disputes "relating to … the Agreement."
- The disputes most likely to arise are grower crop-failure claims, the related indemnity fight and germination claims. These will turn on stand counts, emergence observations, planting and yield data. All of that is Grower Data under DPA §1.3, and DPA §4.1(c) expressly covers "investigating and responding to … Grower Claims."
- Either side can therefore argue for the forum that suits it. The likely results are motion practice over forum, possible parallel proceedings in New York and Iowa, inconsistent rulings and higher cost.
- It is also unclear whether New York law (U.C.C. §1-302(b) and the Issue 2 analysis) or Iowa law governs a mixed dispute.

**Recommended fix.** Use a single law and a single forum for all three documents. On the current paperwork, the cleanest fix is to conform the DPA to the SA:

> **12. Governing Law and Jurisdiction.** This Addendum, and any dispute arising out of or relating to it, is governed by the law and subject to the exclusive forum provided in Section 19.1 of the Agreement. *Section 19.2 of the Agreement does not apply to this Section 12.*

The client may prefer Iowa law and an Iowa forum instead. Sovex is an Iowa LLC based in Ames, and Ludis is in Illinois. In that case, amend SA §19.1 to match and delete the New York choice. **See Open Question 4.** Either way, also amend SA §19.2 to read "the DPA prevails on data protection matters *other than governing law and forum*."

---

### Issue 5: Automatic three-year renewals with a narrow opt-out window

**Where:** SA §2.2.

**What it says.**
- At the end of the Initial Term (**December 31, 2028**), the SA renews automatically for "*successive three (3) year Renewal Terms*."
- Sovex can avoid renewal only by delivering a non-renewal notice "*not more than 150 days* and not less than 120 days" before the end of the then-current Term.
- That is a 30-day window. For the Initial Term it runs from about **August 3 to September 2, 2028**.
- A notice sent too early is as ineffective as one sent too late. Notices take effect on receipt (§18.1).

**Why it matters for Sovex.**
- If Sovex misses the window, it is bound through **December 31, 2031**. That means another three years of:
  - the Minimum Purchase Commitment and shortfall fees (§5), which are uncapped under §12.3(d);
  - the §4.1 exclusivity (Issue 3); and
  - the uncapped indemnity (Issue 1).
- There is no right to terminate for convenience. Termination is available only for breach, insolvency, regulatory change or prolonged force majeure (§15).
- The window falls in late summer, in the middle of the selling season, when it is easy to miss.

**Recommended fix.** Proposed language:

> **2.2 Renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term, this Agreement will renew automatically for successive *one (1) year* Renewal Terms unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal *at least ninety (90) days* before the end of the then-current Term. *In addition, after the Initial Term, Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience on one hundred eighty (180) days' written notice, effective no earlier than the end of the Season then in progress.*

**Interim step:** calendar the August 3 to September 2, 2028 window now, with reminders starting June 2028. Deliver any notice by courier and by email with confirmation of receipt, to the OF2 §8 address.

---

## 3. Other points noted (lower priority)

- **Insurance.** The Broker Letter shows Sovex's CGL meets SA §13.1: $5M per occurrence, insurer rated A/XII (above the A- VII minimum), with an additional-insured endorsement and 30-day cancellation notice. The policies renew January 1, 2027, so a renewal certificate will be due under §13.3. No defect was found, subject to the coverage question in Issue 1.
- **OF2 variety allocation.** The deadline under OF2 §5.3 was November 1, 2026. If Sovex did not give notice, Ludis will allocate pro rata. See Open Question 5.
- **Execution.** The signature blocks in the copies reviewed are blank. Please confirm that fully executed versions of the SA, OF2 and DPA exist.

---

## 4. Open questions for the client

1. **Other seed lines (Issue 3).** Do Sovex or its affiliates currently buy or sell any non-Ludis corn, soybean or sorghum seed, or any seed outside Iowa and Nebraska? The answer determines whether Sovex is already in breach of §4.1 and how urgently the clause must be renegotiated.
2. **Germination testing (Issue 2).** When did Sovex start testing the Order Form No. 1 lots, when did it receive results, and were results available before March 13, 2026? What is the claimed value of the March 30 Claim? Has Ludis responded beyond its April 3 letter?
3. **Grower complaints (Issues 1 and 2).** Have any growers made, or threatened, claims relating to the Order Form No. 1 lots? If so, a §11.3 notice and coverage analysis may be needed now.
4. **Preferred law and forum (Issue 4).** Does Sovex prefer New York or Iowa law and forum for all disputes?
5. **OF2 operational items.** Was the November 1, 2026 variety allocation notice given? Does Sovex expect to meet the 40,000-unit minimum?
6. **Insurance coverage (Issue 1).** Can the broker confirm in writing whether Sovex's CGL would respond to its contractual indemnity of Ludis for grower crop-loss and economic-loss claims? Has Ludis delivered its own certificate naming Sovex as additional insured?
7. **Leverage and timing.** What is the commercial appetite for reopening the SA now? Issues 1 and 2 should ideally be fixed before the first 2027 tranche on January 15, 2027.

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Attorney, Sovex Seed Distribution, LLC matter
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 10, 2026
**Re:** Sovex / Ludis Genetics: review of supply paperwork and recommended pushback

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed four documents:

- the Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2026 (**SA**)
- Order Form No. 2 for the 2026–2027 Season, dated April 20, 2026 (**OF2**)
- the Data Processing Addendum dated January 15, 2026 (**DPA**)
- the February 10, 2026 cover letter from Hartwell Agribusiness Insurance Services enclosing Sovex's certificate of insurance (**Broker Letter**)

**Baseline terms:**

- **Governing law and forum.** The SA is governed by New York law, with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County courts (SA §19.1).
- **Initial Term.** The Initial Term runs to **December 31, 2028** (SA §2.1).
- **Commercial deal.** Under OF2 §2, the deal covers Ludis proprietary hybrid corn listed in Exhibit A. The resale **Territory is Iowa and Nebraska** (OF2 §2.2).
- **OF2 volumes.** OF2 commits Sovex to a 40,000-unit minimum, with a $42/unit shortfall fee (OF2 §§3.2–3.3).

**Main concerns, in order of exposure:**

1. **Uncapped indemnity for all Grower Claims.** Sovex gives an indemnity for all Grower Claims, including claims caused by Ludis's own defective seed, and that indemnity sits outside the liability cap.
2. **Overbroad exclusivity.** The exclusivity clause bars Sovex from carrying any corn, soybean or sorghum seed from other suppliers anywhere in the U.S. and Canada.
3. **Conflicting governing law and forum.** The DPA chooses a competing law and forum (Iowa, Polk County). That clause reaches disputes under the whole Agreement.
4. **Automatic renewal.** The SA renews automatically for three-year terms, with only a 30-day opt-out window.

The Broker Letter is largely in order. It is relevant mainly to how far insurance offsets Item 1.

---

## 2. Issues (ranked by exposure)

### Item 1: Uncapped Customer indemnity covering all Grower Claims, including claims caused by Ludis seed (highest priority)

**Where it appears:**

- SA §11.2 (Customer indemnity)
- SA §1.6 (definition of "Grower Claims")
- SA §12.3(a) (carve-out from the cap)
- SA §12.1 (cap)

**What the documents say:**

- **The indemnity.** Under §11.2, Sovex must defend and indemnify Ludis against any claim "arising out of or relating to Customer's use, handling, storage, resale or planting of Products, *including any Grower Claims*."
- **The definition.** §1.6 defines Grower Claims as any grower claim relating to "crop stand, emergence, yield or performance of Products, **whatever the cause**."
- **The cap.** §12.1 caps each Party's liability at Fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months.
- **The carve-out.** §12.3(a) removes "a Party's obligations under Section 11" from both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion in §12.2.

**Why it matters for Sovex:**

- **Sovex pays for Ludis's defects.** Read together, these provisions make Sovex Ludis's insurer for crop failures, even where the cause is Ludis's nonconforming seed. Examples are low germination, genetic purity problems and seed-treatment defects. Nothing limits the indemnity to Sovex's own fault, such as mishandling, improper storage or off-label statements to growers.
- **The exposure is unlimited.** Because of §12.3(a), the indemnity is not capped. It also escapes the §12.2 exclusion, so it extends to growers' lost profits and lost yield. Crop-loss claims across a two-state, 48,000-unit book could far exceed annual Fees.
- **The carve-out only looks mutual.** §12.3(a) applies to "a Party," but Ludis's only indemnity (§11.1) is a narrow IP-infringement indemnity. In practice, the carve-out benefits Ludis almost entirely.
- **Sovex's own remedies are thin.** §8.6 limits Sovex's remedy against Ludis for nonconforming product to replacement or refund of Fees, and §8.7 disclaims yield warranties. Sovex could therefore pay uncapped grower losses while recovering only the seed price from Ludis.
- **Insurance will probably not close the gap.** Sovex's CGL policy carries a $5,000,000 per-occurrence limit and a $10,000,000 products/completed-operations aggregate (Broker Letter §2.4). Ludis is named as an additional insured as respects the Products (Broker Letter §2.5). However:
  - CGL policies commonly exclude contractually assumed liability, other than "insured contract" coverage.
  - They also commonly exclude "impaired property" and failure-to-perform losses, which is the typical character of yield and stand claims.
  - Grower economic-loss claims may therefore not be covered at all, and limits are finite in any event.

**Recommended fix:**

1. Narrow §11.2 to claims caused by Sovex's own conduct, and expressly exclude claims caused by Ludis's breach or nonconforming Products.
2. Add a reciprocal Supplier indemnity for Grower Claims caused by nonconforming Products.
3. Cap Sovex's indemnity, or at minimum stop it escaping the §12.1 cap.

**Proposed language:**

> **11.2 By Customer.** Customer will defend Supplier … against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) Customer's breach of Section 7.4, 8.8, 10.3 or 10.4, or (b) Customer's negligence or willful misconduct in the handling, storage or resale of Products, including any Grower Claim to the extent so caused. Customer has no obligation under this Section 11.2 for any claim, including any Grower Claim, to the extent arising from (i) Products that did not conform to the warranty in Section 8.1, (ii) Supplier's breach of this Agreement, or (iii) Supplier's negligence or willful misconduct.
>
> **11.1A By Supplier (Product Claims).** Supplier will defend Customer … against any Grower Claim or other third-party claim to the extent arising from Products that did not conform to the warranty in Section 8.1, Supplier's breach of this Agreement, or Supplier's negligence or willful misconduct, and will indemnify them against resulting losses, damages, costs and reasonable attorneys' fees.
>
> **12.3(a)** [replace with:] "Supplier's obligations under Sections 11.1 and 11.1A;"
> and add: "Customer's aggregate liability under Section 11.2 will not exceed [the greater of the Fees paid or payable in the prior twelve (12) months and $[●]]."

**Open questions for the client:**

- Does Sovex currently face any grower complaints or claims about stand or emergence of Ludis seed?
- Has the broker confirmed whether Sovex's CGL responds to contractually assumed grower economic-loss claims?
- Does Sovex's grower paperwork limit grower remedies (for example, to replacement seed or refund)? If it does, that would reduce exposure that flows up to Sovex.

---

### Item 2: Exclusivity far broader than the deal (corn, soybean and sorghum; all of U.S. and Canada)

**Where it appears:**

- SA §4.1
- SA §19.2 (order of precedence)
- OF2 §2 (Products and Territory)

**What the documents say:**

- **The restriction.** §4.1 bars Sovex, directly or through any Affiliate, from purchasing, selling or distributing "any **corn, soybean or sorghum seed** from or on behalf of any person other than Supplier anywhere in **the United States and Canada**."
- **The actual deal.** OF2 §2 limits the deal to Ludis hybrid corn varieties in Exhibit A, resold in the Territory of **Iowa and Nebraska**.
- **Precedence.** §19.2 provides that, outside data protection matters, the SA prevails over the Order Form. The broad §4.1 restriction therefore controls. The narrower Order Form scope does not cut it down.

**Why it matters for Sovex:**

- **Sovex cannot carry other crops or competing corn.** As drafted, Sovex cannot carry competing soybean or sorghum lines, which Ludis does not even supply. Sovex also cannot carry any other company's corn anywhere in North America.
- **It reaches Affiliates.** The restriction would cover any future acquisition or expansion of Sovex outside Iowa and Nebraska, and any Affiliate business.
- **It is not reciprocal.** Ludis's counter-commitment (§4.2) is limited to not appointing other distributors for the Products in the Territory.
- **The lock-in is long.** The restriction runs for the full Term, which, with automatic renewals (Item 4), could be long.
- **Existing breach risk.** If Sovex already sells soybean or sorghum seed from other suppliers, it may be in breach today. That would give Ludis termination leverage under §15.1.
- **Enforceability is uncertain.** Restraints of this breadth may raise antitrust or reasonableness concerns. Sovex should not rely on unenforceability as its strategy; it should get the clause fixed.

**Recommended fix:** Limit exclusivity to directly competing hybrid corn within the Territory, and carve out existing product lines.

**Proposed language:**

> **4.1 Exclusive Purchasing.** During the Term, Customer shall not purchase for resale, or resell, in the Territory any hybrid corn seed of a relative maturity range competitive with the Products listed in Exhibit A to the then-current Order Form, from any person other than Supplier. For clarity, this Section 4.1 does not restrict (a) the purchase, sale or distribution of soybean, sorghum or any other non-corn seed; (b) any activity outside the Territory; (c) any Affiliate of Customer not engaged in the resale of Products; or (d) Customer's sale of [list existing corn brands/lines] in the quantities sold in the [2025] season.

**Open questions for the client:**

- What does Sovex currently carry besides Ludis corn? In particular, does it carry soybean or sorghum lines, or other corn brands?
- Does Sovex or any Affiliate operate outside Iowa and Nebraska, or have plans to?
- This determines whether there is a current breach to manage, in addition to the drafting fix.

---

### Item 3: DPA chooses Iowa law and Polk County courts, and its reach extends to the whole Agreement

**Where it appears:**

- DPA §12 (§§12.1–12.2)
- In conflict with SA §19.1
- Not cured by SA §19.2

**What the documents say:**

- **The DPA choice.** DPA §12.1 provides that the Addendum "and any dispute arising out of or relating to this Addendum, **the Agreement** or any processing of Grower Data" is governed by the **laws of the State of Iowa**. DPA §12.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to courts in **Polk County, Iowa**.
- **The SA choice.** SA §19.1 chooses New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in New York County.
- **Why §19.2 does not resolve it.** SA §19.2 makes the DPA prevail on "data protection matters." The precedence clause therefore does not resolve the conflict in New York's favor. Instead, it arguably gives the Iowa clause effect for any dispute with a data dimension.

**Why it matters for Sovex:**

- **The same dispute may sit in two forums.** Two "exclusive" law and forum clauses compete. Each on its face covers disputes "relating to" the Agreement.
- **Most significant disputes will involve data.** Grower Claims and germination or performance disputes will typically turn on planting, stand count, emergence and yield data, which is Grower Data under DPA §1.3. The DPA expressly contemplates processing Grower Data to investigate Grower Claims (DPA §4.1(c)).
- **Likely consequences:**
  - a threshold fight over which law and court apply
  - possible parallel proceedings in New York and Iowa
  - inconsistent results
  - added cost
- **Iowa is not necessarily the better forum for Sovex.** Iowa may be geographically convenient for Sovex, an Iowa LLC in Ames. But the outcome is uncertain, and Ludis could choose whichever forum suits it.
- **The DPA liability clause loops back to the SA cap.** DPA §13.2 subjects DPA liability to SA §12. The question of which law construes that cap adds further uncertainty.

**Recommended fix:** Conform DPA §12 to SA §19.1, or adopt the client's preferred single forum consistently across all documents. Also tighten §19.2 so it governs only substantive data-protection obligations.

**Proposed language:**

> **DPA 12.1** "This Addendum, and any dispute arising out of or relating to it, is governed by the governing law, and subject to the exclusive forum, stated in Section 19.1 of the Agreement. Nothing in this Section 12 limits the application of Applicable Data Protection Law to the processing of Grower Data." [Delete §12.2.]
>
> **SA 19.2** add: "For clarity, Section 19.1 governs all disputes under this Agreement, any Order Form and the Data Processing Addendum, and the precedence of the Data Processing Addendum on data protection matters does not extend to governing law, jurisdiction or venue."

**Open question for the client:** Does Sovex prefer New York (per the SA) or would it rather litigate in Iowa? If Iowa is preferred commercially, the better fix may be to move *both* documents to Iowa law and an Iowa forum, rather than conforming to New York. Either way, the documents must be made consistent.

### Item 4: Automatic three-year renewals with a 30-day non-renewal window

**Where it appears:** SA §2.2

**What the documents say:**

- **Initial Term.** The Initial Term ends **December 31, 2028** (§2.1).
- **Renewal.** The Agreement then renews automatically "for successive three (3) year Renewal Terms."
- **The opt-out window.** Renewal can be avoided only by written notice delivered "not more than 150 days and not less than 120 days" before the end of the then-current Term. For the Initial Term, that window runs from roughly **August 3, 2028 to September 2, 2028**.
- **Timing of notice.** Notices are effective on receipt (§18.1), so the window is measured by Ludis's receipt, not by when Sovex sends the notice.

**Why it matters for Sovex:**

- **The window is narrow and easily missed.** It is only 30 days, and a notice sent too *early* is also ineffective.
- **Missing it is costly.** Sovex would be locked into three more years (through 2031) of:
  - seasonal Minimum Purchase Commitments with shortfall fees (§§5.1–5.2), which are themselves uncapped under §12.3(d)
  - the overbroad exclusivity in Item 2
  - the uncapped indemnity in Item 1
- **There is no convenience exit.** Sovex has no right to terminate for convenience. Its exit rights are limited to breach, insolvency and regulatory change (§15).

**Recommended fix:**

- Convert to one-year renewals.
- Remove the "not more than 150 days" outer limit so notice can be given at any time before the deadline.
- Add a right for Sovex to terminate on reasonable notice tied to the season cycle.
- In the meantime, **diarize the August 3 – September 2, 2028 window** now, with internal reminders well in advance.

**Proposed language:**

> **2.2 Renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term, this Agreement will renew for successive one (1) year Renewal Terms unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current Term.
>
> **2.4 Termination for Convenience.** After the Initial Term, Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience on at least one hundred twenty (120) days' written notice, effective at the end of a Season; any signed Order Form for a Season then in progress will remain in effect under Section 2.3.

**Open question for the client:** What is Sovex's intended horizon for the Ludis relationship? If Sovex expects a long relationship, it may accept longer renewals in exchange for concessions on Items 1 and 2.
